episodes.title: Big Take 中文摘要｜世界杯谁在买单？
episodes.summary: 2026年世界杯即将在墨西哥拉开帷幕，这是FIFA历史上规模最大的一届，涉及三个主办国和48支参赛队伍。预计赛事总收入将在11亿至13亿美元之间。

sources.title: Who’s Really Paying for This Year’s World Cup?
sources.description: The 2026 World Cup kicks off today in Mexico City. It’ll be the largest in FIFA’s history, spanning three host countries and 48 competing teams and is expected to generate between $11 and $13 billion. But the tournament’s expansion comes at the expense of fans navigating a new dynamic pricing model and cities shouldering overhead costs. On today’s Big Take, host David Gura, Bloomberg’s Vanessa Perdomo and economist Andrew Zimbalist track who stands to profit the most from the people’s game. stories.headline: 谁在买单？
stories.summary: 2026年世界杯的巨额收入分配引起了广泛关注。专家分析指出，虽然球迷们需要适应新的动态定价模式，但城市则承担了额外的成本。
stories.why_it_matters: 了解谁将从这一赛事中获益，对于理解其经济影响至关重要。
